name: Melatonin
route_note: Oral prolonged-release tablets 1–2 hours before bedtime (medicinal products); many immediate-release supplements.
originator: Neurim Pharmaceuticals (Circadin); hormone discovered at Yale

discovery.by: Aaron B. Lerner and colleagues (Yale University)
discovery.note: Isolated from bovine pineal glands as the factor that lightens frog skin melanophores, hence the name.

rx_status: prescription in the EU/UK; dietary supplement (OTC) in the US
tagline: Pineal hormone of darkness, used as a sleep aid and for circadian rhythm disorders
summary: Melatonin is a hormone secreted by the pineal gland at night that signals darkness to the body's circadian system. Prolonged-release melatonin is a licensed medicine in Europe for insomnia in older adults and children with autism or Smith–Magenis syndrome, while in the US it is sold as a dietary supplement.
mechanism: Melatonin activates MT1 and MT2 G-protein-coupled receptors. MT1 activation in the suprachiasmatic nucleus reduces neuronal firing and promotes sleep onset, while MT2 activation shifts the phase of the circadian clock.
Its secretion is suppressed by light via the retinohypothalamic tract; exogenous melatonin can therefore both promote sleepiness and, with timing, advance or delay circadian rhythms.
uses: Primary insomnia in patients aged 55 and over (prolonged-release, EU)
Insomnia in children with autism spectrum disorder or Smith–Magenis syndrome (Slenyto, EU)
Jet lag and circadian rhythm sleep disorders (off-label or supplement use)

history.title: Isolation
history.detail: Aaron Lerner's group isolates melatonin from bovine pineal glands.

history.title: Structure
history.detail: Lerner and colleagues identify the structure as N-acetyl-5-methoxytryptamine.

history.title: US supplement status
history.detail: Under the Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act, melatonin is sold in the US as a supplement.

history.title: Ramelteon
history.detail: The FDA approves ramelteon, a synthetic melatonin receptor agonist, for insomnia.

history.title: Circadin
history.detail: The EMA authorises prolonged-release melatonin for primary insomnia in people aged 55 and over.

history.title: Slenyto
history.detail: A paediatric prolonged-release melatonin is authorised in the EU for children with autism or Smith–Magenis syndrome.

history.title: Supplement content study
history.detail: A JAMA study finds US melatonin gummies often contain amounts differing widely from labels.

pk.half_life: About 40–50 minutes (immediate release); prolonged-release formulations extend exposure

facts: Paediatric melatonin poisonings reported to US poison centres rose sharply between 2012 and 2021, according to the CDC.
